notes:
POC + commercial notes:
- 3-week hosted API POC (chat + embeddings) focused on customer support search + summarization. SE instrumented token burn and KV cache hits.
- Metrics: p50 chat ~120ms, p95 ~185ms during hosted baseline; throughput observed ~120 reqs/min with typical session length ~300 tokens.
- Primary ask: move to Dedicated for predictable SLOs and data isolation. Target steady-state ~50 qps, expected spikes up to 200 qps for marketing/ops bursts. Latency SLO target: p95 <250ms for chats <512 tokens.
- Pricing requirements: clear commit bands (monthly GPU/token commit), burst buffer with deterministic credits, explicit overage rate (prefer flat $/token vs % surcharge). Procurement prefers 12-month reserved with quarterly ramp schedule.
- Proposed commercial structure discussed: Base commit + optional burst pack + 20% discounted overage. AE proposed 30-day ramp (start at 50% commit month1 -> 75% month2 -> 100% month3). Procurement pushing for 60-day ramp and mid-contract re-eval clause.
- Model preferences: customer validated LLaMA-2 and Falcon family; open to Redwood quantized variants. Wants automatic fallback to smaller/8-bit variants when queue grows.
- Security & compliance: require SOC2 type II report, SSO/SAML, KMS integration, audit logging and US-only data residency. Security team submitted questionnaire 2026-03-05 (answers pending).
- Legal asks: SLO credits for missed latency targets, clear termination/redress if major performance regressions after model upgrades, indemnity language around data handling.
- Stakeholder quotes: "We need cost certainty — no surprise GPU overages." — VP Product; "If Dedicated gives predictable p95, we can commit." — CTO.
- Current action items: SE to model token burn per session and validate cache hit assumptions; commercial to produce two formal pricing bundles (Conservative & Aggressive) with burst terms and overage math; legal to circulate redline draft.
- Risk notes: internal forecasting conservative; finance may insist on monthly spend caps. If ramp schedule not acceptable, deal could slip to Q3.
